correctness.rationale: On K_(n,n) each synchronous non-lazy step samples a uniformly independent vertex of the opposite side; two part-specific coupon streams are independent. Different-part starts yield U_(n,1)(t)^2; distinct same-part starts yield U_(n,0)(2s)U_(n,2)(2s) even, U_(n,0)(2s+2)U_(n,2)(2s) odd. Exact reveal identities U0(m+1)=U1(m), U1(m+1)=U1(m)/n+(n−1)U2(m)/n establish positive odd difference U1(m+1)(U1(m+1)−U1(m))/(n−1) for m>=n−2. Even first missing-coupon terms cancel, leaving rho^(2m)+O(q^m), q=1−2/n<rho²; asymptotic ratio 1. Enumerated coupon sequences n=2..5 and checked exact alternating CDFs for s=1..7; some early even differences are zero (e.g. n=4,s=1), correctly distinguished from eventual strict inequalities. Collocated starts pathwise dominated by distinct same-part, preventing any randomized global stochastic optimum.

value.rationale: Full deadline-by-deadline stochastic order is a natural risk-sensitive cover-time criterion not captured by expected speedup. An infinite, vertex-transitive bipartite family has perpetual late-time parity crossings and proves no deterministic or randomized universally optimal starting arrangement. Sharp differing tail rates explain the obstruction structurally.
